newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin informed of Clinton's election victory.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin informed of Clinton's election victory.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, recovering on Wednesday after heart surgery, is to send a message of congratulation to Bill Clinton on his U.S. presidential election win, Kremlin sources said.
Cited by Interfax news agency, the sources said Yeltsin had been informed of the election result in his hospital bed. The two leaders enjoy cordial relations.
Russian foreign policy experts say the Kremlin will have been relieved at Clinton's victory as it prefers continuity and has less confidence in the Republicans.
Russians in the street have generally shown little interest in the U.S. election campaign, absorbed as they are with their own economic and political crises and Yeltsin's health.

In a recently opened McDonald's hamburger joint in central Moscow, Jan, a 26-year-old Russian busy serving behind a spotless stainless-steel counter, said he welcomed Clinton's victory. "I would've voted for him -- he's young and he looks good," he said.

"We congratulate him, we like and believe him," said 38-year-old builder Valery Popov between bites on a large hamburger. "Clinton built better relations with Russia than the Republicans did," he said.
A soldier friend of his, 35-year old Valery, said the Cold War was dead and gone and that Americans had nothing to fear from Russia.
"We can't win in Chechnya so how could we ever beat America?" he said in reference to the bloody war in the breakaway republic in southern Russia.
A senior Russian diplomat quoted by Interfax, however, said the NATO alliance's plans to expand eastwards in Europe could muddy relations.
